title_en: Regulations on the Prevention and Control of Forest Pests and Diseases

articles.content_en: These Regulations are formulated in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Forest Law of the People's Republic of China to effectively prevent and control forest pests and diseases, protect forest resources, promote forestry development, and maintain natural ecological balance.

For the purposes of these Regulations, prevention and control of forest pests and diseases means the prevention and elimination of diseases and insect pests of forests, trees, forest seedlings, timber and bamboo.
The policy of 'prevention first, integrated management' shall be implemented for the prevention and control of forest pests and diseases.

The responsibility system of 'whoever manages, prevents and controls' shall be implemented for the prevention and control of forest pests and diseases.
Local people's governments at all levels shall formulate measures and systems to strengthen leadership over the prevention and control of forest pests and diseases.

The forestry department under the State Council shall be in charge of the prevention and control of forest pests and diseases nationwide.
The forestry departments of local people's governments at or above the county level shall be in charge of the prevention and control of forest pests and diseases within their respective administrative regions, and the forest pest and disease prevention and control institutions affiliated to them shall be responsible for the specific organizational work of forest pest and disease prevention and control.
Forestry workstations of districts and townships shall be responsible for organizing the prevention and control of forest pests and diseases in their respective districts and townships.

The State shall encourage and support scientific research on the prevention and control of forest pests and diseases, and promote and apply advanced technologies to improve the level of scientific prevention and control.

The forestry departments of people's governments at all levels shall, in a planned manner, organize the establishment of forest seedling bases free of quarantine objects. The forest pest and disease prevention and control institutions at all levels shall, according to law, carry out origin and transit quarantine for forest seedlings, timber and bamboo; where newly introduced dangerous pests and diseases are discovered, they shall promptly take strict measures for sealing off and eradication, and shall not transfer the dangerous pests and diseases outside.
Animal and plant quarantine institutions at various ports shall, in accordance with the legal provisions of the State on the quarantine of animals and plants entering and leaving the country, strengthen the quarantine of inbound forest seedlings, timber and bamboo, and prevent the introduction of forest pests and diseases from abroad.

The forestry departments of people's governments at all levels shall organize and supervise forest management entities and individuals to take effective measures to protect various beneficial organisms in forests, and to propagate and cultivate them in a planned manner, so as to give full play to the role of biological control.

The forest pest and disease prevention and control institutions of the forestry department under the State Council and of the forestry departments of the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall comprehensively analyze the forecast data from various sources, regularly issue respectively national and regional medium- and long-term trend forecasts for forest pests and diseases, and propose prevention and control plans.
The forestry departments of the people's governments of counties, cities and autonomous prefectures, or the forest pest and disease prevention and control institutions affiliated to them, shall comprehensively analyze the forecast data from grass-roots units, issue local short- and medium-term forecasts for forest pests and diseases, and propose prevention and control plans.
For forests and trees owned by the whole people, the state-owned forestry bureaus, state-owned forest farms or other management entities shall organize investigations into the situation of forest pests and diseases.
For forests and trees owned by collectives or individuals, the forestry workstations of districts and townships or the county forest pest and disease prevention and control institutions shall organize investigations into the situation of forest pests and diseases.
Each investigating unit shall report the investigation results on forest pests and diseases to the superior forestry department or its forest pest and disease prevention and control institution in accordance with the provisions.

The forestry department under the State Council shall be responsible for formulating the forecast objects and methods for major forest pests and diseases; the forestry departments of the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions and municipalities directly under the Central Government may make supplementary provisions in light of the conditions in their respective administrative regions, and shall submit them to the forestry department under the State Council for recordation.
The forest pest and disease prevention and control institutions of the forestry department under the State Council and of the forestry departments of provinces, autonomous regions and municipalities directly under the Central Government may establish central forecast stations in different areas according to actual needs to conduct investigation and monitoring of forecast objects.

The forestry departments of local people's governments at all levels shall, in areas where forest pests and diseases frequently occur, implement comprehensive management measures that combine forestry measures with biological, chemical and physical control, gradually improve the forest ecological environment, and enhance the forest's ability to resist natural disasters.

Entities and individuals that discover severe forest pests and diseases shall promptly report to the local people's government or forestry department.
Upon receiving the report, the local people's government or forestry department shall promptly organize elimination and simultaneously report to the forestry department of the people's government of the province, autonomous region or municipality directly under the Central Government.
Where a large-scale outbreak or dangerous forest pests and diseases occur, the forestry department of the people's government of the province, autonomous region or municipality directly under the Central Government shall promptly report to the forestry department under the State Council.

Where outbreak or dangerous forest pests and diseases occur, the local people's government shall, according to actual needs, organize relevant departments to establish a temporary command organization for prevention and control of forest pests and diseases, which shall be responsible for formulating emergency elimination measures and coordinating to resolve major problems in the work.

Local people's governments at or above the county level or their forestry departments shall formulate implementation plans for the elimination of forest pests and diseases, organize joint prevention and control in border areas, and conduct regular inspections of the elimination situation.

The application of pesticides must comply with relevant regulations to prevent environmental pollution, ensure the safety of humans and livestock, and reduce the killing of beneficial organisms.
Where aircraft are used for pesticide application, the local forestry department of the people's government shall conduct prior investigation and design, and make proper ground preparations; the forestry, civil aviation and meteorological departments shall closely cooperate to ensure the quality of operations.

When severe forest pests and diseases occur, commercial, supply and marketing, materials, petrochemical and other departments shall give priority to the supply of necessary pesticides, equipment, fuel, etc.; railway, transportation and civil aviation departments shall give priority to transportation; and civil aviation departments shall give priority to arranging aircraft for pesticide application.

For expenses on prevention and control of forest pests and diseases, for forests and trees owned by the whole people, they shall be met from the forest cultivation fund, timber and bamboo sales revenue, diversified business income and operating expenses in accordance with relevant state regulations; for forests and trees owned by collectives or individuals, the expenses shall be borne by the operators, and local people's governments at all levels may provide appropriate support.
For forest management entities and individuals whose forests and trees have no economic income temporarily or for a long period, such as protection forests, water source forests and forests for special uses, the expenses required for prevention and control of forest pests and diseases shall be appropriately supported by local people's governments at all levels.
Where a large-scale outbreak or dangerous pests and diseases occur, and forest management entities or individuals are truly unable to bear all the prevention and control expenses, people's governments at all levels shall provide subsidies.

The State shall gradually implement a forest pest and disease insurance system in key forest areas, and the specific measures shall be formulated by the People's Insurance Company of China in conjunction with the forestry department under the State Council.

Whoever, in violation of plant quarantine laws and regulations, transports forest seedlings or timber shall, in addition to being punished in accordance with the plant quarantine laws and regulations, also be fined not less than 50 yuan but not more than 2,000 yuan.

The persons responsible for the acts specified in Articles 22 and 23 of these Regulations, or State functionaries who have neglected their duties in the prevention and control of forest pests and diseases, shall be given administrative sanctions by their units or higher authorities; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated by the judicial organs according to law.

If the person ordered to eliminate forest pests and diseases within a time limit fails to do so, the forestry department or an authorized unit may eliminate them on their behalf, and the person ordered to eliminate shall bear all prevention and control expenses.
The work of eliminating forest pests and diseases on behalf of the person shall not be suspended due to the person's application for reconsideration or prosecution.

The administrative penalties prescribed in these Regulations shall be decided by the forestry departments of people's governments at or above the county level or by units authorized by them.
If a party is dissatisfied with the decision on administrative penalty, it may, within 15 days from the date of receipt of the penalty notification, apply for reconsideration to the authority at the next higher level over the authority that made the decision; if dissatisfied with the reconsideration decision, it may, within 15 days from the date of receipt of the reconsideration decision document, file a lawsuit with the People's Court. The party may also directly file a lawsuit with the People's Court within 15 days from the date of receipt of the penalty notification. If, upon expiration of the time limit, no application for reconsideration or lawsuit has been filed and the penalty decision is not complied with, the authority that made the penalty decision shall apply to the People's Court for compulsory execution.
These Regulations shall be interpreted by the forestry department under the State Council.

The people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions and municipalities directly under the Central Government may, in light of these Regulations and their local actual conditions, formulate implementing measures.

For forests and trees managed by urban landscape management departments, the prevention and control of pests and diseases shall be implemented by the urban landscape management departments with reference to these Regulations.
These Regulations shall come into force as of the date of promulgation.
